change.title: pr-90939-flat
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: No re-check of the cache after taking the write lock
findings.body: On a cold or failed cache in non-dev mode, every concurrent caller passes the RLock check with `ret == nil`. Each then takes `Lock()` in turn and re-reads and parses `assets-manifest.json` (and may do the CDN HTTP request), even though the first caller has already filled `entryPointAssetsCache`. Add the usual double-check after line 49: `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`. The lock is also held during file and network I/O, so in Dev mode every call takes the exclusive lock and requests are serialized. That is acceptable for dev, but the double-check is cheap and makes the non-dev path correct. The `data race` is fixed as intended; this is only redundant work.

contracts.action: GetWebAssets now guards the package-level entryPointAssetsCache with an RWMutex (read under RLock, write under Lock)
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous unsynchronized read and write of entryPointAssetsCache in the same function
contracts.before_after: Before: unguarded read of the global, then an unguarded write at the end, which is a data race under concurrent requests. After: the read is under RLock, and the manifest load and the write are under Lock with a deferred Unlock. The fast path for a warm non-dev cache is unchanged, apart from the RLock. The slow path has no re-check after Lock, so concurrent cold callers each reload the manifest.
contracts.visible_effect: The returned assets reach the index template as before. There is no change in output; the only difference is the removed race and redundant reloads under contention.
contracts.failure_mode: If the manifest load fails, result is nil, the cache is set to nil and the error is returned. This is the same as before, and the next call retries. The deferred Unlock releases the lock even on panic. The ctx passed to the CDN read is cancelable, but cdn is hard-coded to "" so that branch is currently dead.

summary: The mutex fixes the data race on `entryPointAssetsCache`, and the failure behavior is unchanged. The only issue is a missing double-check after taking the write lock, so concurrent cold callers each reload the manifest. I rate it as a minor perf point.
